literal: Unable to endure closing, suffering grief, my eyes, which caused the love-sickness exceeding the ocean.
translation: My very eyes, which brought upon me this love-sickness greater than the ocean, are now suffering from grief, unable even to close in sleep.
modern: கடலை விடப் பெரிய காம நோயை எனக்கு உண்டாக்கிய என் கண்கள், இப்போது தூங்குவதற்குக் கூட முடியாமல் துன்பத்தை அனுபவிக்கின்றன.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the irony of her situation. It was her own eyes that first gazed upon her lover and created a passion so vast that even the ocean cannot contain it (கடல் ஆற்றா காமநோய்). Now, those very same eyes are unable to close (படல் ஆற்றா) in sleep and must endure the agonizing grief of separation. The poet beautifully contrasts the active role of the eyes in creating the desire with their current passive suffering.
